findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply... Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available"
findings.fix: Rewrite as one conjunctive sentence, e.g., "The stipend is available only when the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each sentence states the stipend "can apply" based on a single condition alone, but the final sentence requires all three conditions jointly - the individual and cumulative framings contradict each other.

findings.evidence: "If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply."
findings.fix: Add an explicit definition of "benefit year."
findings.violation: "Benefit year" is never defined anywhere in the document (calendar year, fiscal year, hire-date anniversary?), making this eligibility condition unverifiable.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove the anecdote or replace it with a general rule for backup-reviewer coverage during manager absences.
findings.violation: This is a narrative anecdote describing a one-off operational failure, not a general policy rule, and is out of place in a procedural policy document.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days."
findings.fix: Either remove the contradictory anecdote in "How to Apply" or add an explicit exception to the two-day SLA for reviewer unavailability.
findings.violation: This firm SLA directly contradicts the preceding "How to Apply" section, which describes review being delayed indefinitely because the untrained backup reviewer didn't know sign-off was required.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Remove the discretion clause or clarify how it interacts with the Eligibility section, and include or link the referenced checklist.
findings.violation: This grants unbounded discretionary approval that conflicts with the fixed, rule-based Eligibility criteria, and references a "standard review checklist" that is never described anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence or replace it with "The deposit reimburses costs the employee has already paid."
findings.violation: "At this point in time" is meaningless filler, and the sentence is redundant with the prior sentence describing the deposit.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request an annual photo check."
findings.violation: This switches to second person ("you," "we"), inconsistent with the third-person voice ("the employee," "the manager") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" and define the equipment categories the one-per-category rule applies to.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this follows logically from the prior photo-check sentence, but the two are unrelated; additionally, "category" is never defined anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: "The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year" vs. "the policy applies to one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: State explicitly whether $500 is a total annual cap or a per-category cap.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section (vs. Reimbursement Amounts)
findings.violation: It is unclear whether the $500 cap applies per category or as a single total across all categories, since combining multiple categories with a per-category device limit could multiply the effective stipend.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Either add actual definitions of terms (e.g., "stipend item," "benefit year," "category") or delete the section as redundant.
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" contains no term definitions; it repeats process steps already covered in "How to Apply" and "Program Coordination," and switches to second person inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Identify one authoritative owner and timeline for disbursement and remove the conflicting statements.
findings.violation: This introduces a third disbursing party and cadence ("Payroll," "monthly review") that conflicts with "Reimbursement Amounts" ("The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle") and "Program Coordination" ("the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle").

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this into "How to Apply" or expand it into a complete list of steps.
findings.violation: This near-duplicates the "How to Apply" section with far less detail, and the heading implies a fuller sequence than the two items given.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Merge the two overview sections and state a single owner and cadence for the reimbursement log.
findings.violation: This contradicts "Program Overview" at the top of the document, which states "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" - different owner and different cadence for the same artifact.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.violation: This sentence is a verbatim duplicate of a sentence already used in "Program Overview" in a different context, indicating unedited, duplicated content and a redundant duplicate "Overview" heading.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Clarify which team is actually responsible for scheduling and executing the deposit.
findings.violation: This assigns disbursement scheduling to the benefits team, contradicting "Reimbursement Amounts," which assigns the deposit action to the finance office.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate this finance review step into the Approval Timeline section so the order of all review steps is clear.
findings.violation: This introduces an additional, threshold-based review gate that is not mentioned in "Approval Timeline," leaving the full approval sequence (manager review, this finance review, and the "internal discretion" clause) undefined and out of order.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Rename the section to match its content (e.g., "Vendor List Publication") and add an actual section addressing how employees ask questions or receive policy updates.
findings.violation: The content has nothing to do with questions or updates and introduces an undefined new artifact ("vendor list") that is never referenced or explained elsewhere in the document.
